source_caption:
Growing Up Smith follows a young Indian-American boy growing up in 1970s America who develops a crush on a girl from a wealthy white family. As he navigates cultural expectations, family traditions, and his desire to fit in, he learns about identity, love, and growing up.

The film is a coming-of-age romantic comedy directed by Frank Lotito. It stars Roni Akurati, Brighton Sharbino, Jason Lee, and Anjul Nigam, exploring cultural differences, family relationships, and the challenges of adolescence.

source_details.title: Growing Up Smith
source_details.synopsis: Growing Up Smith is a 2015 comedy-drama film written by Anjul Nigam, Paul Quinn, and Gregory Scott Houghton. It was produced by Anjul Nigam, Frank Lotito, and Steve Straka and directed by Frank Lotito. The movie takes place in 1979, when an Indian family moves to America with hopes of living the American Dream. While their 10-year-old boy Smith falls head-over-heels for the girl next door, his desire to become a "good old boy" propels him further away from his family's ideals than ever before.
